Find the probability that a randomly selected member of the group

parts.text:
(a) always eats breakfast and takes regular exercise,
(2)

NB $\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{2}{3}$ alone or $\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{9}{25}$ alone scores M0A0. Correct answer scores full marks.

(2)
(b) does not always eat breakfast and does not take regular exercise.
(4)

(2)

questions.stem:
In a shopping survey a random sample of 104 teenagers were asked how many hours, to the nearest hour, they spent shopping in the last month.  The results are summarised in the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Number of hours} & \text{Mid-point} & \text{Frequency}\\ \hline 0-5 & 2.75 & 20\\ \hline 6-7 & 6.5 & 16\\ \hline 8-10 & 9 & 18\\ \hline 11-15 & 13 & 25\\ \hline 16-25 & 20.5 & 15\\ \hline 26-50 & 38 & 10\\ \hline\end{array}$

A histogram was drawn and the group $(8-10)$ hours was represented by a rectangle that was 1.5 cm wide and 3 cm high.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Calculate the width and height of the rectangle representing the group $(16-25)$ hours.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) 8-10 hours: width = $10.5-7.5=3$ represented by 1.5cm; 16-25 hours: width = $25.5-15.5=10$ so represented by 5 cm B1. 8-10 hours: height = fd $=18/3=6$ represented by 3 cm; 16-25 hours: height = fd $=15/10=1.5$ represented by 0.75 cm M1 A1. M1: For attempting both frequency densities $\frac{18}{3}(=6)$ and $\frac{15}{10}$, and $\frac{15}{10}\times \mathrm{SF}$, where $\mathrm{SF}\neq1$. NB Wrong class widths (2 and 9) gives $\frac{h}{1.66\ldots}=\frac{3}{9}\to h=\frac{5}{9}$ or 0.55… and scores M1A0.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median and interquartile range.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $Q_2=7.5+\frac{(52-36)}{18}\times3=10.2$ M1 A1. $Q_1=5.5+\frac{(26-20)}{16}\times2[=6.25\text{ or }6.3]$ or $5.5+\frac{(26.25-20)}{16}\times2[=6.3]$ A1. $Q_3=10.5+\frac{(78-54)}{25}\times5[=15.3]$ or $10.5+\frac{(78.75-54)}{25}\times5[=15.45/15.5]$ A1ft. IQR $=(15.3-6.3)=9$ A1ft. M1: for identifying correct interval and a correct fraction e.g. $\frac{\frac{1}{2}(104)-36}{18}$. Condone 52.5 or 53. 1st A1: for 10.2 for median. Using $(n+1)$ allow awrt 10.3. NB: must see some method. 2nd A1: for a correct expression for either $Q_1$ or $Q_3$ (allow 26.25 and 78.75). 3rd A1: for correct expressions for both $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. 4th A1ft: for IQR, ft their quartiles. Using $(n+1)$ gives 6.28 and 15.45.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Estimate the mean and standard deviation of the number of hours spent shopping.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $\sum fx=1333.5\Rightarrow \bar{x}=\frac{1333.5}{104}=$ AWRT 12.8 M1 A1. $\sum fx^2=27254\Rightarrow \sigma_x=\sqrt{\frac{27254}{104}-\bar{x}^2}=\sqrt{262.05-\bar{x}^2}=$ AWRT 9.88 M1 A1. 1st M1: for attempting $\sum fx$ and $\bar{x}$. 2nd M1: for attempting $\sum fx^2$ and $\sigma_x$, $\sqrt{\ }$ is needed for M1. Allow $s=$ awrt 9.93.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) State, giving a reason, the skewness of these data.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) $Q_3-Q_2[=5.1]>Q_2-Q_1[=3.9]$ or $Q_2<\bar{x}$ B1ft. So data is positively skew dB1. 1st B1ft: for suitable test, values need not be seen but statement must be compatible with values used. Follow through their values. 2nd dB1: Dependent upon their test showing positive and for stating positive skew. If their test shows negative skew they can score 1st B1 but lose the second.

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) State, giving a reason, which average and measure of dispersion you would recommend to use to summarise these data.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) Use median and IQR, since data is skewed or not affected by extreme values or outliers B1 B1. 1st B1: for choosing median and IQR. Must mention both. 2nd B1: for suitable reason. e.g. "use median because data is skewed" scores B0B1 since IQR is not mentioned.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Award independently

questions.stem: The random variable $X$ has a normal distribution with mean 30 and standard deviation 5.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{P}(X<39)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{39-30}{5}\right)$ M1: for standardising with $\sigma$, $z=\pm\frac{39-30}{5}$ is OK. $=\mathrm{P}(Z<1.8)=0.9641$ (allow awrt 0.964) A1. Answer only scores all marks in each section BUT check (b) and (c) are in correct order.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- A1 for 0.9641 or awrt 0.964 but if they go on to calculate 1 – 0.9641 they get M1A0

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the value of $d$ such that $\mathrm{P}(X<d)=0.1151$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $\mathrm{P}(X<d)=\mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{d-30}{5}\right)=0.1151$ M1: for attempting $1-0.1151$. Must be seen in (b) in connection with finding $d$. $1-0.1151=0.8849$ (allow $\pm1.2$) B1: for $z=\pm1.2$. They must state $z=\pm1.2$ or imply it is a $z$ value by its use. This mark is only available in part (b). $\Rightarrow z=-1.2$; $\therefore \frac{d-30}{5}=-1.2$ M1: for $\left(\frac{d-30}{5}\right)=$ their negative $z$ value (or equivalent). A1: $d=24$.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the value of $e$ such that $\mathrm{P}(X>e)=0.1151$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) $\mathrm{P}(X>e)=0.1151$ so $e=\mu+(\mu-\text{their }d)$ or $\frac{e-30}{5}=1.2$ or $-$ their $z$ M1: for a full method to find $e$. If they used $z=1.2$ in (b) they can get M1 for $z=\pm1.2$ here. If they use symmetry about the mean $\mu+(\mu-\text{their }d)$ then ft their $d$ for M1. Must explicitly see the method used unless the answer is correct. A1: $e=36$.

parts.label: d
parts.mark_scheme: (d) $\mathrm{P}(d<X<e)=1-2\times0.1151$ M1: for a complete method or use of a correct expression e.g. "their 0.8849" $-0.1151$ or, if their $d<$ their $e$, using their values with $\mathrm{P}(X<e)-\mathrm{P}(X<d)$. If their $d\geqslant$ their $e$ then they can only score from an argument like $1-2\times0.1151$. A negative probability or probability $>1$ for part (d) scores M0A0. $=0.7698$ AWRT $0.770$ A1.
